# infisical_secret_validation_rule (Resource)

Create and manage secret validation rules in an Infisical project. Validation rules enforce constraints on static secret keys and values, and on the credentials generated by dynamic secrets and secret rotations. Infisical rejects rules whose scope and constraints overlap an existing rule of the same type, so use `depends_on` between rules that share an environment and secret path to keep applies deterministic. Only Machine Identity authentication is supported for this resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    infisical = {
      # version = <latest version>
      source = "infisical/infisical"
    }
  }
}

provider "infisical" {
  host = "https://app.infisical.com" # Only required if using self hosted instance of Infisical, default is https://app.infisical.com
  auth = {
    universal = {
      client_id     = "<machine-identity-client-id>"
      client_secret = "<machine-identity-client-secret>"
    }
  }
}

resource "infisical_project" "example" {
  name = "example"
  slug = "example"
}

# Enforce naming and strength requirements on static secrets in production.
resource "infisical_secret_validation_rule" "prod_static_secrets" {
  project_id       = infisical_project.example.id
  name             = "production-secret-standards"
  description      = "Naming and strength requirements for production secrets"
  environment_slug = "prod"
  secret_path      = "/**"

  rule = {
    type = "static-secrets"
    constraints = [
      {
        type       = "required-prefix"
        applies_to = "key"
        value      = "PROD_"
      },
      {
        type       = "min-length"
        applies_to = "value"
        value      = "16"
      },
      {
        type       = "prevent-value-reuse"
        applies_to = "value"
        value      = "5"
      },
    ]
  }
}

# Constrain the passwords generated by dynamic secret leases. Omitting environment_slug
# applies the rule to every environment in the project.
resource "infisical_secret_validation_rule" "dynamic_secret_passwords" {
  project_id  = infisical_project.example.id
  name        = "dynamic-secret-password-policy"
  secret_path = "/**"

  rule = {
    type      = "dynamic-secrets"
    providers = ["sql-database"]
    constraints = [
      {
        type       = "min-length"
        applies_to = "password"
        value      = "24"
      },
    ]
  }
}

# Stage a secret rotation password policy without enforcing it yet.
resource "infisical_secret_validation_rule" "rotation_passwords" {
  project_id  = infisical_project.example.id
  name        = "rotation-password-policy"
  secret_path = "/services/**"
  is_active   = false

  rule = {
    type      = "secret-rotations"
    providers = ["postgres-credentials"]
    constraints = [
      {
        type       = "regex-pattern"
        applies_to = "password"
        value      = "^[A-Za-z0-9]{32}$"
      },
    ]
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the secret validation rule
- `project_id` (String) The ID of the project the secret validation rule belongs to
- `rule` (Attributes) The rule configuration. The type field selects which kind of secret the constraints apply to. Infisical replaces the rule configuration as a whole on update. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rule))
- `secret_path` (String) The secret path the rule applies to. Supports glob patterns, e.g. "/", "/prod", "/prod/**".

### Optional

- `description` (String) An optional description of the secret validation rule. Infisical trims surrounding whitespace, so avoid whitespace-only values.
- `environment_slug` (String) The slug of the environment to scope the rule to. When omitted, the rule applies to all environments in the project.
- `is_active` (Boolean) Whether the rule is enforced. Defaults to true. Set to false to keep the rule but stop enforcing it.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the secret validation rule

<a id="nestedatt--rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule`

Required:

- `constraints` (Attributes Set) The constraints enforced by this rule. At least one constraint is required. Order is not significant. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rule--constraints))
- `type` (String) The kind of secret the rule applies to. Possible values: static-secrets, dynamic-secrets, secret-rotations

Optional:

- `providers` (Set of String) The dynamic secret or secret rotation providers the rule applies to, e.g. "sql-database" or "postgres-credentials". Required when type is `dynamic-secrets` or `secret-rotations`

<a id="nestedatt--rule--constraints"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule.constraints`

Required:

- `applies_to` (String) What the constraint applies to. Possible values: key, value, password. Static secret rules support `key` and `value`, while dynamic secret and secret rotation rules support `password` only.
- `type` (String) The constraint type. Possible values: min-length, max-length, regex-pattern, required-prefix, required-suffix, prevent-value-reuse
- `value` (String) The constraint value, always expressed as a string. For `min-length` and `max-length` this is a number, for `regex-pattern` a regular expression, and for `prevent-value-reuse` the number of previous versions to check.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# Import a secret validation rule using its project ID and rule ID
terraform import infisical_secret_validation_rule.example <project_id>,<rule_id>
```
